svg.text: COPPER SIDE, mirrored: what you see when you cut the tracks
26 × 42 holes · cut to 66.0 × 106.7 mm · 34 cuts · 49 links · 2 standoff holes (2.5 mm, for M2.5 nylon standoffs)
Take the Pi’s header once, on a keyed ribbon, and give each board its own keyed cable.
Connectors (pin 1 is the large filled square)
D1 → Core: Pi 5 (vip), 2×20 IDC box header: 1 the Pi’s 40-pin header, one
D2 → Codec carrier, Molex KK 254 14-way: 1 GND · 2 BCLK · 3 GND · 4 LRCLK
(DACLRC) · 5 GND · 6 ADCDAT · 7 GND · 8 DACDAT · 9 GND · 10 SDA · 11 SCL ·
D3 → Control: Pico 2 WH, JST-XH 4-way (B4B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 Pico TX (GP0) →
Pi RXD, pin 10 · 3 Pico RX (GP1) ← Pi TXD, pin 8 · 4 +5 V hold
GND reaches the root through D1 only (Core: Pi 5 (vip)).
One 40-way box header, cut between its two rows on every strip — a knife
cut, because the pins are 2.54 mm apart and a spot cutter will not fit. The
ribbon plugs in once; everything else unplugs here.
D2 is the 14-way KK header the codec carrier takes. Its grounds are six of
the Pi’s own ground pins, one beside each clock and data wire.
LINK’s 5 V is pin 4, so the codec’s VIN keeps pin 2. They are the same rail
on the Pi; the separate pins are only so the two leads do not share a
The test points are the header pins themselves: BCLK is pin 12, LRCLK pin
35, ADCDAT pin 38, DACDAT pin 40, SDA pin 3 and SCL pin 5. A Qwiic port, if
it is wanted, taps those same I2C pins; it is not drawn.

Red ✕: cut the track at that hole (red bar: cut between two holes). Lines: wire links on the component side (green carries ground). Strips tinted green carry ground, red a supply, amber 3.3 V. White circles: standoff holes; dashed: what the standoff covers.
